10	
11	The product brief (`datatracemind_product_brief.md`, Section 4, "Model
12	access") records why this route was chosen. This file is the operational
13	reference; if the two differ on how to call Codex, this file wins.
14	
15	------------------------------------------------------------------------
16	
17	## 1. What this is
18	
19	DataTraceMind's agent roles get their model through the **Codex CLI in
20	non-interactive mode** (`codex exec`), authenticated by the ChatGPT
21	sign-in already present on the machine. No OpenAI API key is required.
22	
23	Codex is an **agent called one turn at a time**, not a chat-completions
24	endpoint. Do not look for a base URL, a chat client, or function-call
25	objects returned to our code. There is no supported way to get an
26	OpenAI-compatible API billed to a ChatGPT plan, and proxies that reuse
27	the login token are not to be used.
28	
29	| Need | How it is met |
30	|---|---|
31	| Prompt in, response out | `codex exec "<prompt>"` returns a final message |
32	| Typed output | `--output-schema <file>` forces the final message to match a JSON Schema |
33	| Tool calling | Our tools are served to Codex by one MCP server; Codex runs the tool loop itself |
34	| Agent workflow | Each LLM-backed role is one Codex turn; the supervisor is a plain Python state machine |
35	
36	Consequences: LangGraph/LangChain chat-model integrations and
37	`neatlogs.wrap(<client>)` do not apply. The provider is used in exactly
38	one place, the LLM adapter in the FastAPI agent service.
39	
40	------------------------------------------------------------------------
41	
42	## 2. Fixed model settings
43	
44	| Setting | Value | How it is passed |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| Model | `gpt-6-sol` (the mid-tier model, between `gpt-6-luna` and `gpt-6-astra`) | `-m gpt-6-sol` |
47	| Reasoning effort | `medium` | `-c 'model_reasoning_effort="medium"'` |
48	
49	-   Pass both explicitly on every call, together with
50	    `--ignore-user-config`. Never rely on `~/.codex/config.toml`: it is
51	    personal, differs between machines, and currently sets a different
52	    effort on the team leader's laptop.
53	-   Keep both as named constants in the adapter. Changing either makes
54	    earlier runs incomparable, so record any change, with the reason, in
55	    `hackathon.md` and in the trace's `workflow_version` label.
56	
57	------------------------------------------------------------------------
58	
59	## 3. The command
60	
61	Every model call uses this form. It is verified as written.
62	
63	``` sh
64	codex exec --json --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --ignore-user-config \
65	  -m gpt-6-sol -c 'model_reasoning_effort="medium"' \
66	  -s read-only -C "$EMPTY_WORKDIR" \
67	  --disable shell_tool -c 'web_search="disabled"' \
68	  -c 'mcp_servers.dtm.command="/abs/path/to/python"' \
69	  -c 'mcp_servers.dtm.args=["/abs/path/to/mcp_server.py"]' \
70	  -c 'mcp_servers.dtm.required=true' \
71	  -c 'mcp_servers.dtm.default_tools_approval_mode="approve"' \
72	  -c 'mcp_servers.dtm.enabled_tools=["tool_a","tool_b"]' \
73	  --output-schema "$ROLE_SCHEMA_JSON" \
74	  "$ROLE_PROMPT" < /dev/null
75	```
76	
77	| Part | Purpose | What happens without it |
78	|---|---|---|
79	| `--json` | Emit one JSON event per line on stdout | Only the final text is printed; tool calls and token usage are lost |
80	| `--ephemeral` | Do not persist session files | Session files accumulate in `~/.codex` |
81	| `--skip-git-repo-check` | Allow running outside a Git repository | Codex requires a Git repository by default, and the working directory is not one |
82	| `--ignore-user-config` | Ignore `~/.codex/config.toml`; sign-in is still used | Behaviour depends on each machine's personal config |
83	| `-s read-only` | Sandbox with no writes | Read-only is already the `codex exec` default; stating it guards against a changed default |
84	| `-C "$EMPTY_WORKDIR"` | Working root is an empty directory | Codex starts in the caller's directory and picks up that project's files and instructions |
85	| `--disable shell_tool` | Remove Codex's shell | The model can run commands and read any file, including `.env` and scenario ground truth |
86	| `web_search="disabled"` | Remove web search | Web search may be available to the model |
87	| `mcp_servers.dtm.required=true` | Fail the run if the tool server does not start | Codex continues with no tools and invents an answer |
88	| `default_tools_approval_mode="approve"` | Pre-approve tool calls | Every tool call fails with "MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never" |
89	| `enabled_tools=[...]` | Allow-list of tools for this role | The role can call every tool on the server |
90	| `--output-schema` | Typed final message | Free-form text |
91	| `< /dev/null` | Close stdin | `codex exec` prints "Reading additional input from stdin..." and waits forever |
92	
93	Notes:
94	
95	-   `-c` values are parsed as TOML, so strings need inner double quotes
96	    and lists use TOML syntax. Use absolute paths.
97	-   A long prompt can be sent on stdin instead of as an argument (then
98	    do not redirect from `/dev/null`). Only the argument form is
99	    verified.
100	-   Never use `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`,
101	    `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`, `-s danger-full-access`, or
102	    `-s workspace-write` for an agent role.
103	
104	------------------------------------------------------------------------
105	
106	## 4. Reading the output
107	
108	With `--json`, stdout is JSON Lines. Shapes observed:
109	
110	``` json
111	{"type":"thread.started","thread_id":"01a12491-..."}
112	{"type":"turn.started"}
113	{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_0","type":"agent_message","text":"I'll query the refund status profile..."}}
114	{"type":"item.started","item":{"id":"item_1","type":"mcp_tool_call","server":"dtm","tool":"profile_refunds_by_status","arguments":{},"result":null,"error":null,"status":"in_progress"}}
115	{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_1","type":"mcp_tool_call","server":"dtm","tool":"profile_refunds_by_status","arguments":{},"result":{"content":[...],"structured_content":{"result":[...]}},"error":null,"status":"completed"}}
116	{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_2","type":"agent_message","text":"{\"succeeded_refund_amount\":37150,...}"}}
117	{"type":"turn.completed","usage":{"input_tokens":34239,"cached_input_tokens":22272,"cache_write_input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":130,"reasoning_output_tokens":8}}
118	```
119	
120	-   **Final answer:** the `text` of the **last** `agent_message`. With
121	    `--output-schema` it is a JSON string. Earlier `agent_message` items
122	    are narration; ignore them.
123	-   **Tool calls:** every `item.completed` whose item type is
124	    `mcp_tool_call`. A successful call has `status: "completed"` and
125	    `error: null`. A failed call has `status: "failed"` and
126	    `error.message`. A tool that returns a list arrives as
127	    `structured_content.result`.
128	-   **Token usage:** `turn.completed.usage`, one total for the turn.
129	-   **Failure events:** `turn.failed` and `error`. Other item types
130	    (`reasoning`, and others in the Codex docs) can appear; skip unknown
131	    types instead of failing on them.
132	-   **Exit code 0 does not mean success.** A run whose tool call failed
133	    still exited 0 with a schema-valid answer. See Section 6.
134	-   Progress text goes to stderr. Capture it for debugging; do not parse
135	    it.
136	
137	------------------------------------------------------------------------
138	
139	## 5. Tools: the MCP server
140	
141	The investigation and repair tools (product brief, Section 11) are
142	exposed to Codex by one stdio MCP server named `dtm`.
143	
144	-   **Library:** the Python `mcp` package, version 2.x. Use
145	    `from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer`, decorate tools with
146	    `@mcp.tool()`, and call `mcp.run()`. The 1.x import
147	    `mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` on 2.x.
148	-   **Lifetime:** Codex starts the server as a subprocess for each turn
149	    and stops it afterwards. Tools must not depend on state kept in the
150	    server process between turns; read and write through the database.
151	-   **Timeouts (Codex defaults):** 10 s for server start
152	    (`startup_timeout_sec`) and 60 s per tool call (`tool_timeout_sec`).
153	    Keep server imports light.
154	-   **Per-role allow-list:** pass `enabled_tools` for the role. Tools
155	    not listed do not exist for that turn.
156	-   **Configuration and credentials** reach the server through
157	    `mcp_servers.dtm.env` (documented by Codex; not yet tested here).
158	    Give it the read-only database credentials only.
159	-   **Descriptions matter:** the tool's docstring and parameter names
160	    are what the model sees. State what the tool returns and its units.
161	-   Investigation tools are read-only. No tool may accept free-form SQL
162	    from the model; use query templates with typed parameters.
163	
164	------------------------------------------------------------------------
165	
166	## 6. Rules the adapter must enforce
167	
168	1.  **Verify the tool calls, not the prose.** Each role declares the
169	    tools it must call. Fail the turn unless each has at least one
170	    `mcp_tool_call` with `status: "completed"` and `error: null`. Twice
171	    in testing, with the tool missing or blocked, Codex still returned a
172	    schema-valid answer containing an invented value (`0`).
173	2.  **Build evidence from recorded tool results.** Evidence objects come
174	    from `structured_content` in the event stream (or from the server's
175	    own record), never from the model's summary of a result.
176	3.  **Validate the final message again in Python** against the role's
177	    Pydantic model. Treat a parse or validation error as a failed turn.
178	4.  **Bound every call.** Enforce a subprocess timeout, kill the process
179	    on expiry, and retry a failed turn a fixed small number of times
180	    before escalating the incident.
181	5.  **Prompts are fixed templates filled from typed state.** No text
182	    typed by a user of the web application may reach a prompt. This is
183	    what makes a public URL acceptable (Section 7).
184	6.  **Check authentication before starting a run** (Section 7) and
185	    refuse with a clear message instead of failing mid-investigation.
186	7.  **Deterministic checks still decide.** Codex proposes; staging
187	    validation, approval, and post-fix verification are code. A Codex
188	    statement that something passed or was approved proves nothing.
189	
190	------------------------------------------------------------------------
191	
192	## 7. Authentication and where the agent may run
193	
194	Codex credentials are per machine and per person. There is no
195	unauthenticated way to call a model.
196	
197	| Machine | How it authenticates | Billing |
198	|---|---|---|
199	| Team leader's laptop | `codex login` (browser sign-in), already done | ChatGPT Plus allowance |
200	| A teammate's machine | Their own `codex login` | Their own plan |
201	| EC2 instance (live URL) | Team leader runs `codex login --device-auth` on the instance and approves in a browser elsewhere | The same Plus allowance |
202	| Fallback, any machine | `CODEX_API_KEY` set to an OpenAI Platform API key | Per token, to that API account |
203	
204	-   **Preflight:** `codex login status` exits `0` when signed in and `1`
205	    when not (verified). The agent service is "available" if that
206	    passes or `CODEX_API_KEY` is set. Expose the result to the
207	    dashboard.
208	-   **No credentials:** the application still starts. Simulator, ETL,
209	    detection, staging validation, approval, and audit work without a
210	    model. Starting an investigation is refused with a message naming
211	    the fix. Never substitute a canned diagnosis.
212	-   **`~/.codex/auth.json` is a password.** Never commit it, copy it
213	    between machines, bake it into an image, print it, or paste it into
214	    a chat or a coding-agent session. On EC2 it lives in a `CODEX_HOME`
215	    directory readable only by the agent service's user and mounted into
216	    the agent container.
217	-   **Device sign-in** is a beta feature that must be enabled in the
218	    ChatGPT account's security settings first. Signing in, enabling that
219	    setting, and creating an API key are human-only steps.
220	-   **`CODEX_API_KEY`** is an ordinary OpenAI API key, separate from the
221	    ChatGPT subscription, which includes no API credit. It needs no code
222	    change: set it in the instance's `.env` and restart the agent.
223	-   **Public URL guardrails:** fixed prompts only (rule 5), a demo
224	    access code for inject/investigate/approve, a cap on investigations
225	    per hour and per day, only ports 80/443 open to the world.
226	
227	------------------------------------------------------------------------
228	
229	## 8. Cost, speed, and limits
230	
231	-   **Overhead:** each model round trip carries Codex's own
232	    instructions. Observed: about 14,000 input tokens for a turn with no
233	    tool call, and about 34,000 (22,000 of them cached) for a turn with
234	    one tool call. Keep roles few and turns short.
235	-   **Latency:** 6--16 s per turn in testing, including one tool call.
236	-   **Plus allowance:** OpenAI's published estimate is 15--150 local
237	    messages per five hours on `gpt-6-sol`; weekly limits may also
238	    apply. Each role turn is one message. The allowance is shared by
239	    local development, the live URL, and any Codex coding the team does.
240	-   **Dollar figures:** Plus is flat-rate, so there is no real cost per
241	    call. For the business plan, compute an estimate from measured token
242	    counts at API list prices and label it as an estimate. Prices
243	    published on 10 October 2026, per million tokens (input / cached
244	    input / output): `gpt-6-sol` \$2.00 / \$0.20 / \$10.00;
245	    `gpt-6-luna` \$0.10 / \$0.01 / \$0.50.
246	
247	------------------------------------------------------------------------
248	
249	## 9. Tracing with neatlogs
250	
251	neatlogs tracing is a hackathon requirement and goes through
252	`datatracemind/observability/`.
253	
254	-   Model calls happen inside the Codex process, so there are no
255	    automatic model spans. Wrap each Codex turn in an agent span
256	    (`@neatlogs.span(kind="AGENT")`) inside `investigation_run(...)`, and
257	    record the role, model, reasoning effort, token usage, duration, and
258	    Codex `thread_id` on it.
259	-   The MCP server is a separate process, so spans created there do not
260	    join the run's trace by themselves. Either create one tool span per
261	    `mcp_tool_call` event in the adapter, or pass trace context to the
262	    server (`neatlogs.inject_trace_context` on our side,
263	    `neatlogs.extract_trace_context` in the server). Neither is built or
264	    tested yet.
265	-   The `@neatlogs/codex` hooks package is installed globally on the
266	    team leader's machine. It runs only after its hooks are trusted in
267	    Codex (`/hooks`), and whether it captures `codex exec` runs is
268	    untested. It is optional; do not depend on it.
269	
270	------------------------------------------------------------------------
271	
272	## 10. Verified and not verified
273	
274	| Claim | Status |
275	|---|---|
276	| `codex exec` works non-interactively on the ChatGPT Plus sign-in | Verified |
277	| `--output-schema` returns schema-valid JSON as the last `agent_message` | Verified |
278	| MCP tool call succeeds with `default_tools_approval_mode="approve"` | Verified (confirmed server-side) |
279	| Tool call is refused without that setting | Verified |
280	| `--disable shell_tool` removes the shell | Verified (model reported it had no way to run commands) |
281	| `enabled_tools`, `required`, `--ignore-user-config`, `-m gpt-6-sol`, medium effort, all together | Verified |
282	| `codex exec` hangs when stdin is left open | Verified |
283	| Codex answers with an invented value when a tool is unavailable | Verified, twice |
284	| `codex login status` exit codes 0 and 1 | Verified |
285	| `CODEX_API_KEY` authenticates `codex exec` | From Codex docs; not tested |
286	| `codex login --device-auth` on a headless machine | From Codex docs; not tested |
287	| `mcp_servers.<id>.env` passes environment to the server | From Codex docs; not tested |
288	| Prompt delivered on stdin | From CLI help; not tested |
289	| Behaviour on Linux and inside a container | Not tested |
290	| `disabled_tools`, `tool_timeout_sec`, `startup_timeout_sec` | From Codex docs; not tested |
291	| neatlogs Codex hooks capture `codex exec` | Not tested |
292	
293	When you verify or disprove a row, update this table.
294	
295	------------------------------------------------------------------------
296	
297	## 11. Adapter contract
298	
299	Keep the adapter's interface free of Codex specifics so that another
300	provider could replace it by changing one module.
301	
302	**In**
303	
304	-   Role name.
305	-   Prompt: a fixed template filled from typed incident state.
306	-   Allowed tools and required tools for the role.
307	-   Output schema (a Pydantic model; its JSON Schema is written to a
308	    file for `--output-schema`). Use strict schemas: every property
309	    listed in `required` and `additionalProperties: false`. That is the
310	    form verified.
311	
312	**Out**
313	
314	-   The validated result object.
315	-   The tool-call record: tool, arguments, structured result, status,
316	    error.
317	-   Token usage, duration, and the Codex `thread_id`.
318	-   An error type that distinguishes: not authenticated, timed out, tool
319	    server failed to start, required tool not called or failed, invalid
320	    final message, usage limit reached.
321	
322	Sources: Codex CLI help (`codex exec --help`, `codex login --help`),
323	the Codex documentation on non-interactive mode, authentication, the
324	configuration reference, and pricing, and probes run on 10 October 2026.
325

``` json
{"type":"thread.started","thread_id":"01a12491-..."}
{"type":"turn.started"}
{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_0","type":"agent_message","text":"I'll query the refund status profile..."}}
{"type":"item.started","item":{"id":"item_1","type":"mcp_tool_call","server":"dtm","tool":"profile_refunds_by_status","arguments":{},"result":null,"error":null,"status":"in_progress"}}
{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_1","type":"mcp_tool_call","server":"dtm","tool":"profile_refunds_by_status","arguments":{},"result":{"content":[...],"structured_content":{"result":[...]}},"error":null,"status":"completed"}}
{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_2","type":"agent_message","text":"{\"succeeded_refund_amount\":37150,...}"}}
{"type":"turn.completed","usage":{"input_tokens":34239,"cached_input_tokens":22272,"cache_write_input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":130,"reasoning_output_tokens":8}}
```

-   **Final answer:** the `text` of the **last** `agent_message`. With
    `--output-schema` it is a JSON string. Earlier `agent_message` items
    are narration; ignore them.
-   **Tool calls:** every `item.completed` whose item type is
    `mcp_tool_call`. A successful call has `status: "completed"` and
    `error: null`. A failed call has `status: "failed"` and
    `error.message`. A tool that returns a list arrives as
    `structured_content.result`.
-   **Token usage:** `turn.completed.usage`, one total for the turn.
-   **Failure events:** `turn.failed` and `error`. Other item types
    (`reasoning`, and others in the Codex docs) can appear; skip unknown
    types instead of failing on them.
-   **Exit code 0 does not mean success.** A run whose tool call failed
    still exited 0 with a schema-valid answer. See Section 6.
-   Progress text goes to stderr. Capture it for debugging; do not parse
    it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. Tools: the MCP server

The investigation and repair tools (product brief, Section 11) are
exposed to Codex by one stdio MCP server named `dtm`.

-   **Library:** the Python `mcp` package, version 2.x. Use
    `from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer`, decorate tools with
    `@mcp.tool()`, and call `mcp.run()`. The 1.x import
    `mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` on 2.x.
-   **Lifetime:** Codex starts the server as a subprocess for each turn
    and stops it afterwards. Tools must not depend on state kept in the
    server process between turns; read and write through the database.
-   **Timeouts (Codex defaults):** 10 s for server start
    (`startup_timeout_sec`) and 60 s per tool call (`tool_timeout_sec`).
    Keep server imports light.
-   **Per-role allow-list:** pass `enabled_tools` for the role. Tools
    not listed do not exist for that turn.
-   **Configuration and credentials** reach the server through
    `mcp_servers.dtm.env` (documented by Codex; not yet tested here).
    Give it the read-only database credentials only.
-   **Descriptions matter:** the tool's docstring and parameter names
    are what the model sees. State what the tool returns and its units.
-   Investigation tools are read-only. No tool may accept free-form SQL
    from the model; use query templates with typed parameters.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 6. Rules the adapter must enforce

1.  **Verify the tool calls, not the prose.** Each role declares the
    tools it must call. Fail the turn unless each has at least one
    `mcp_tool_call` with `status: "completed"` and `error: null`. Twice
    in testing, with the tool missing or blocked, Codex still returned a
    schema-valid answer containing an invented value (`0`).
2.  **Build evidence from recorded tool results.** Evidence objects come
    from `structured_content` in the event stream (or from the server's
    own record), never from the model's summary of a result.
3.  **Validate the final message again in Python** against the role's
    Pydantic model. Treat a parse or validation error as a failed turn.
4.  **Bound every call.** Enforce a subprocess timeout, kill the process
    on expiry, and retry a failed turn a fixed small number of times
    before escalating the incident.
5.  **Prompts are fixed templates filled from typed state.** No text
    typed by a user of the web application may reach a prompt. This is
    what makes a public URL acceptable (Section 7).
6.  **Check authentication before starting a run** (Section 7) and
    refuse with a clear message instead of failing mid-investigation.
7.  **Deterministic checks still decide.** Codex proposes; staging
    validation, approval, and post-fix verification are code. A Codex
    statement that something passed or was approved proves nothing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 7. Authentication and where the agent may run

Codex credentials are per machine and per person. There is no
unauthenticated way to call a model.

| Machine | How it authenticates | Billing |
|---|---|---|
| Team leader's laptop | `codex login` (browser sign-in), already done | ChatGPT Plus allowance |
| A teammate's machine | Their own `codex login` | Their own plan |
| EC2 instance (live URL) | Team leader runs `codex login --device-auth` on the instance and approves in a browser elsewhere | The same Plus allowance |
| Fallback, any machine | `CODEX_API_KEY` set to an OpenAI Platform API key | Per token, to that API account |

-   **Preflight:** `codex login status` exits `0` when signed in and `1`
    when not (verified). The agent service is "available" if that
    passes or `CODEX_API_KEY` is set. Expose the result to the
    dashboard.
-   **No credentials:** the application still starts. Simulator, ETL,
    detection, staging validation, approval, and audit work without a
    model. Starting an investigation is refused with a message naming
    the fix. Never substitute a canned diagnosis.
-   **`~/.codex/auth.json` is a password.** Never commit it, copy it
    between machines, bake it into an image, print it, or paste it into
    a chat or a coding-agent session. On EC2 it lives in a `CODEX_HOME`
    directory readable only by the agent service's user and mounted into
    the agent container.
-   **Device sign-in** is a beta feature that must be enabled in the
    ChatGPT account's security settings first. Signing in, enabling that
    setting, and creating an API key are human-only steps.
-   **`CODEX_API_KEY`** is an ordinary OpenAI API key, separate from the
    ChatGPT subscription, which includes no API credit. It needs no code
    change: set it in the instance's `.env` and restart the agent.
-   **Public URL guardrails:** fixed prompts only (rule 5), a demo
    access code for inject/investigate/approve, a cap on investigations
    per hour and per day, only ports 80/443 open to the world.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 8. Cost, speed, and limits

-   **Overhead:** each model round trip carries Codex's own
    instructions. Observed: about 14,000 input tokens for a turn with no
    tool call, and about 34,000 (22,000 of them cached) for a turn with
    one tool call. Keep roles few and turns short.
-   **Latency:** 6--16 s per turn in testing, including one tool call.
-   **Plus allowance:** OpenAI's published estimate is 15--150 local
    messages per five hours on `gpt-6-sol`; weekly limits may also
    apply. Each role turn is one message. The allowance is shared by
    local development, the live URL, and any Codex coding the team does.
-   **Dollar figures:** Plus is flat-rate, so there is no real cost per
    call. For the business plan, compute an estimate from measured token
    counts at API list prices and label it as an estimate. Prices
    published on 10 October 2026, per million tokens (input / cached
    input / output): `gpt-6-sol` \$2.00 / \$0.20 / \$10.00;
    `gpt-6-luna` \$0.10 / \$0.01 / \$0.50.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 9. Tracing with neatlogs

neatlogs tracing is a hackathon requirement and goes through
`datatracemind/observability/`.

-   Model calls happen inside the Codex process, so there are no
    automatic model spans. Wrap each Codex turn in an agent span
    (`@neatlogs.span(kind="AGENT")`) inside `investigation_run(...)`, and
    record the role, model, reasoning effort, token usage, duration, and
    Codex `thread_id` on it.
-   The MCP server is a separate process, so spans created there do not
    join the run's trace by themselves. Either create one tool span per
    `mcp_tool_call` event in the adapter, or pass trace context to the
    server (`neatlogs.inject_trace_context` on our side,
    `neatlogs.extract_trace_context` in the server). Neither is built or
    tested yet.
-   The `@neatlogs/codex` hooks package is installed globally on the
    team leader's machine. It runs only after its hooks are trusted in
    Codex (`/hooks`), and whether it captures `codex exec` runs is
    untested. It is optional; do not depend on it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 10. Verified and not verified

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| `codex exec` works non-interactively on the ChatGPT Plus sign-in | Verified |
| `--output-schema` returns schema-valid JSON as the last `agent_message` | Verified |
| MCP tool call succeeds with `default_tools_approval_mode="approve"` | Verified (confirmed server-side) |
| Tool call is refused without that setting | Verified |
| `--disable shell_tool` removes the shell | Verified (model reported it had no way to run commands) |
| `enabled_tools`, `required`, `--ignore-user-config`, `-m gpt-6-sol`, medium effort, all together | Verified |
| `codex exec` hangs when stdin is left open | Verified |
| Codex answers with an invented value when a tool is unavailable | Verified, twice |
| `codex login status` exit codes 0 and 1 | Verified |
| `CODEX_API_KEY` authenticates `codex exec` | From Codex docs; not tested |
| `codex login --device-auth` on a headless machine | From Codex docs; not tested |
| `mcp_servers.<id>.env` passes environment to the server | From Codex docs; not tested |
| Prompt delivered on stdin | From CLI help; not tested |
| Behaviour on Linux and inside a container | Not tested |
| `disabled_tools`, `tool_timeout_sec`, `startup_timeout_sec` | From Codex docs; not tested |
| neatlogs Codex hooks capture `codex exec` | Not tested |

When you verify or disprove a row, update this table.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 11. Adapter contract

Keep the adapter's interface free of Codex specifics so that another
provider could replace it by changing one module.

**In**

-   Role name.
-   Prompt: a fixed template filled from typed incident state.
-   Allowed tools and required tools for the role.
-   Output schema (a Pydantic model; its JSON Schema is written to a
    file for `--output-schema`). Use strict schemas: every property
    listed in `required` and `additionalProperties: false`. That is the
    form verified.

**Out**

-   The validated result object.
-   The tool-call record: tool, arguments, structured result, status,
    error.
-   Token usage, duration, and the Codex `thread_id`.
-   An error type that distinguishes: not authenticated, timed out, tool
    server failed to start, required tool not called or failed, invalid
    final message, usage limit reached.

Sources: Codex CLI help (`codex exec --help`, `codex login --help`),
the Codex documentation on non-interactive mode, authentication, the
configuration reference, and pricing, and probes run on 10 October 2026.

"""neatlogs tracing for the DataTraceMind agent workflow.

Every model call and every agent tool call must appear in a neatlogs trace
(product brief, Section 4). Tracing is evidence, not control flow: nothing
here may stop an incident from being investigated, so a missing key or a
failed export degrades to "not traced" instead of raising.

Usage:
    init_tracing()                    # once, at process start, before any
                                      # LLM client or agent framework import
    client = wrap_llm_client(Provider())
    with investigation_run(incident_id, scenario_id=..., version=...) as trace_id:
        ...                           # @neatlogs.span roles and tools nest here
    shutdown_tracing()                # once, at process exit
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
from collections.abc import Iterator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Any

import neatlogs
from dotenv import load_dotenv

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

WORKFLOW_NAME = "datatracemind"

_initialized = False


def init_tracing(*, tags: list[str] | None = None) -> bool:
    """Start neatlogs export. Returns False when runs will not be traced."""
    global _initialized
    if _initialized:
        return True
    # The SDK reads os.environ only; .env has to be loaded before init().
    load_dotenv()
    api_key = os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY")
    if not api_key:
        logger.warning("NEATLOGS_API_KEY is not set; agent runs will not be traced")
        return False
    try:
        neatlogs.init(api_key=api_key, workflow_name=WORKFLOW_NAME, tags=tags)
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("neatlogs.init failed; agent runs will not be traced")
        return False
    _initialized = True
    return True


def shutdown_tracing() -> None:
    """Send buffered spans and stop the exporter.

    Call once at exit (FastAPI lifespan shutdown, or the end of a script).
    Short scripts that skip this can exit before their trace is sent.
    """
    global _initialized
    if not _initialized:
        return
    neatlogs.flush()
    neatlogs.shutdown()
    _initialized = False


def wrap_llm_client(client: Any, **workflow_attributes: Any) -> Any:
    """Return `client` with every call traced.

    The LLM adapter builds its provider client through this function and
    nowhere else, so no model call can bypass tracing.
    """
    if not _initialized:
        return client
    return neatlogs.wrap(client, **workflow_attributes)


def langchain_handler() -> Any:
    """Callback handler for a LangGraph/LangChain run.

    Create one per investigation run and pass it at the graph invocation
    (config={"callbacks": [handler]}), not on individual node calls.
    """
    return neatlogs.langchain_handler()


def current_trace_id() -> str | None:
    """Hex ID of the active trace, or None outside a traced run."""
    # neatlogs keeps its active span on a private context key, so the OTel
    # global current-span is empty. Its W3C traceparent header
    # ("00-<trace_id>-<span_id>-<flags>") is the supported way to read it.
    carrier: dict[str, str] = {}
    if not neatlogs.inject_trace_context(carrier):
        return None
    return carrier["traceparent"].split("-")[1]


@contextmanager
def investigation_run(
    incident_id: str,
    *,
    scenario_id: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
) -> Iterator[str | None]:
    """Root span for one investigation run; yields its trace ID.

    Role and tool spans opened inside nest under it. The incident ID is also
    the neatlogs session ID, so every run for an incident (first attempt,
    re-investigation after a failed validation, post-fix verification) is
    grouped together. `version` labels the workflow/prompt revision, which is
    what makes a before/after pair of runs comparable.
    """
    attributes = {"incident_id": incident_id}
    if scenario_id is not None:
        attributes["scenario_id"] = scenario_id
    if version is not None:
        # Not trace(version=...): that only versions prompt templates and
        # leaves nothing on the span to search or compare by.
        attributes["workflow_version"] = version
    with neatlogs.trace(
        "investigation_run",
        kind="WORKFLOW",
        session_id=incident_id,
        **attributes,
    ):
        yield current_trace_id()

1	# cfo.ai Connectors
2	
3	Reference for coding agents and teammates who build the cfo.ai business
4	plan for DataTraceMind or consider connecting anything to cfo.ai. Read
5	it before adding a cfo.ai connection, exporting cost data for the plan,
6	or exposing any DataTraceMind endpoint to cfo.ai.
7	
8	**Status:** explored 10 October 2026 in the team leader's cfo.ai
9	workspace and the public cfo.ai docs. The path in Section 5 is a
10	**recommendation, not yet a decision**; when the team leader decides,
11	record it here and in `hackathon.md`. Nothing was connected or changed
12	in the workspace during the exploration. Section 9 lists what is
13	verified and what is not.
14	
15	The product brief (`datatracemind_product_brief.md`, Section 4,
16	"cfo.ai --- business plan") defines what the plan must cover. This file
17	covers how data can reach cfo.ai. It does not change the brief's rule
18	that the product has no runtime integration with cfo.ai.
19	
20	------------------------------------------------------------------------
21	
22	## 1. Summary
23	
24	-   The connector we would want, **PostgreSQL, is not available**: it is
25	    a Premium integration and this workspace's plan does not include
26	    Premium. **ClickHouse is not in the catalog at all.**
27	-   Three routes do work on this plan: cfo.ai's own MCP server (a coding
28	    agent reads and edits the model), CSV upload, and a custom API
29	    connection.
30	-   **Recommended:** the MCP server plus a CSV of per-investigation
31	    cost. The plan is then built from measured numbers instead of typed
32	    ones, which is what the brief asks for and what the 25% tooling
33	    score rewards.
34	-   The custom API connection is a stretch goal, only after DS-01 works
35	    end to end and the live URL is up.
36	
37	------------------------------------------------------------------------
38	
39	## 2. The workspace
40	
41	| Item | Observed 10 October 2026 |
42	|---|---|
43	| Workspace | "Divine Joey" (slug `divine-joey-f38178b9`) |
44	| Plan | Startup, on its trial; shown as Canceled, ends 24 October 2026 |
45	| Integration slots | Standard 0 of 5 used; "Premium not included" |
46	| Included AI usage | 0% used; resets 24 October 2026 |
47	| Extra usage | Purchased balance \$0.00; auto-reload off; monthly spend limit \$500.00 |
48	| Connections | None |
49	
50	-   The trial ends after winners are announced on 16 October, so the
51	    workspace stays usable through judging. Per the cfo.ai billing docs,
52	    cancelling keeps the Model and its data; when the trial ends the
53	    workspace returns to the plan chooser.
54	-   The Startup plan, per the pricing page: up to 5 standard
55	    integrations, up to 500,000 rows synced per month, and the MCP
56	    server included.
57	-   Billing controls are human-only. Do not press **Keep Startup**,
58	    **Change**, **Buy credits**, or **Adjust limit**, and leave
59	    **Auto-reload** off.
60	
61	------------------------------------------------------------------------
62	
63	## 3. Connection types
64	
65	The connection manager opens from the sidebar (**Connections → +**) and
66	from **Settings → Connections**. It has three tabs and an **Upload**
67	button. cfo.ai's own MCP server is a fifth route that runs in the other
68	direction.
69	
70	| Type | Where | How data arrives | Uses a plan slot |
71	|---|---|---|---|
72	| Integration | **Integrations** tab | Synced into the Model nightly, in a shared run that starts at 02:00 UTC | Yes |
73	| File upload | **Upload** button | One-off import of a `.csv`; never refreshes on its own | No |
74	| MCP connector | **MCP** tab | Ari calls the server live when asked; nothing is synced | No |
75	| API connection | **API** tab | Ari calls the API live when asked; nothing is synced | No |
76	| cfo.ai MCP server | Outside the app, at `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp` | An external agent reads and edits the Model | No; included in Startup |
77	
78	-   **Integrations:** at most 100 tables per connection, and the table
79	    selection cannot be changed after setup. There is no manual refresh
80	    button; Ari can refresh a connection on request.
81	-   **Live connections (MCP, API):** a figure Ari looks up can be
82	    written into a Table Block as a plain value. It does not update
83	    afterwards.
84	-   **Secrets** for a connection are typed by a human into the secure
85	    field on the connection card. They are never pasted into the chat
86	    with Ari or into a coding-agent session.
87	
88	------------------------------------------------------------------------
89	
90	## 4. Fit for DataTraceMind
91	
92	| Connector | Fit | Reason |
93	|---|---|---|
94	| cfo.ai MCP server | **Use** | Builds pricing, costs, revenue, and runway from the coding agent, with base and growth as Scenarios |
95	| CSV upload | **Use** | Free, no slot, and carries measured cost per investigation into the Model |
96	| Custom API connection | Stretch | The FastAPI service can serve an OpenAPI document, so Ari could query a read-only cost endpoint on the live URL |
97	| Google Sheets | Possible, not planned | Standard, one slot, nightly refresh; more moving parts than CSV for no demo gain |
98	| PostgreSQL (also RDS, Aurora, Cloud SQL, Azure, Heroku) | **Blocked** | Tagged Premium in the catalog; the plan shows "Premium not included" |
99	| ClickHouse | **Not available** | Searching the catalog returns "No integrations found" |
100	| Custom MCP server pointing at `dtm` | **Do not use** | See Section 7 |
101	| Stripe, QuickBooks, HubSpot, and similar | Not relevant | The simulator has no real accounts behind it |
102	
103	Even on a plan with Premium, the PostgreSQL connector would suit this
104	project poorly: it syncs once a night through Fivetran and needs a
105	database reachable from the internet, while ours runs in local Docker
106	Compose.
107	
108	------------------------------------------------------------------------
109	
110	## 5. Recommended path
111	
112	### 5.1 cfo.ai MCP server
113	
114	A coding agent connects to cfo.ai and builds the plan in the workspace.
115	This is a **development-time tool only**, like Entire. Never add it to
116	the `codex exec` invocation used by agent roles (see
117	`CODEX_LLM_PROVIDER.md`, Section 3); the product does not call cfo.ai.
118	
119	| Setting | Value |
120	|---|---|
121	| Server name | `cfoai` |
122	| URL | `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp` |
123	| Transport | Remote Streamable HTTP |
124	| Authentication | OAuth in the browser, with the cfo.ai account |
125	
126	``` sh
127	# Claude Code: then start claude, open /mcp, select cfoai, Authenticate
128	claude mcp add --transport http cfoai https://api.cfo.ai/mcp
129	
130	# Codex
131	codex mcp add cfoai --url https://api.cfo.ai/mcp
132	codex mcp login cfoai
133	```
134	
135	The browser sign-in and approval are human-only steps (Section 8).
136	
137	-   **Workspace:** with one workspace the connection uses it. Otherwise
138	    call `list_orgs` and pass the workspace ID or slug as `org_id` on
139	    every later call.
140	-   **Read tools named in the docs:** `list_orgs`,
141	    `inspect_table_blocks`, `inspect_pages`, `inspect_scenarios`,
142	    `inspect_integrations`, `inspect_skills`, `inspect_canvas_library`,
143	    `inspect_dimension_mappings`, `inspect_history`,
144	    `inspect_documentation`.
145	-   **Write tools named in the docs:** `edit_table_blocks` (all model
146	    formulas go through it), `edit_pages`, `edit_scenarios`,
147	    `edit_dimension_mappings`, `edit_canvas_blocks`,
148	    `edit_integrations`, `edit_triggers`.
149	-   The cfo.ai docs pages do not list exactly the same tools. After
150	    sign-in, read the names and schemas from the server itself and
151	    follow <https://docs.cfo.ai/agent-instructions.md>.
152	-   **Call shape:** multi-action tools take one block named for the
153	    action, for example `{"read": {"target": "Operating Plan"}}`. There
154	    is no flat `action` field. One `read` takes up to 16 targets.
155	
156	Rules when writing to the Model:
157	
158	1.  **Inspect before changing.** Read the existing Model and the
159	    `build-model` skill (`inspect_skills`) first. Setup needs no writes;
160	    an empty workspace is a valid first read.
161	2.  **Writes change the live Model.** There is no separate approval
162	    step, so make only the change that was asked for.
163	3.  **Main is the base case.** Put the growth case in a separate
164	    Scenario (`edit_scenarios`), not in Main. That gives the two revenue
165	    scenarios the brief requires.
166	4.  **Label measured against assumed.** Cost per investigation comes
167	    from Section 5.2. Pricing, customer counts, and growth rates are
168	    assumptions and must be named as such in the Model.
169	5.  **Keep the evidence.** Export the plan or take screenshots into
170	    `business-plan/`, and note the session in `hackathon.md`.
171	
172	A session that uses this server is captured by Entire like any other,
173	and checkpoints in a public repository are public. The plan is a
174	submission artifact, so that is acceptable; keep tokens out of the
175	session.
176	
177	### 5.2 CSV of measured cost
178	
179	The brief requires inference cost per investigation to come from real
180	runs. A small script exports one row per investigation, and a human
181	uploads the file.
182	
183	-   **Source:** the token usage in each Codex turn's `turn.completed`
184	    event, summed per investigation (the same figures recorded on the
185	    neatlogs agent spans).
186	-   **Dollar figure:** an estimate at API list prices, computed as in
187	    `CODEX_LLM_PROVIDER.md`, Section 8. Name the column so that the
188	    estimate is obvious, for example `est_cost_usd`.
189	-   **Suggested columns:** `run_date`, `incident_id`, `scenario_id`,
190	    `workflow_version`, `role_turns`, `input_tokens`,
191	    `cached_input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `est_cost_usd`,
192	    `duration_s`.
193	-   **How cfo.ai reads columns:** numeric columns become summed
194	    Variables; text columns become Dimensions; a numeric column whose
195	    name marks an identifier (for example one ending in "id") loads as a
196	    text Dimension. Date columns are read per whole column.
197	-   **Upload:** the file must have a `.csv` extension and be at most
198	    50 MB. Choose **Use as a data source**, not **Use in chat only**.
199	    An Excel workbook is not accepted as a data source.
200	-   **Refresh:** uploads never refresh. They are tracked by filename;
201	    upload the file again to update it. Ingestion runs in the
202	    background, so ask Ari whether loading has finished.
203	-   Send summaries only: no source rows, customer data, prompts, or
204	    secrets.
205	
206	------------------------------------------------------------------------
207	
208	## 6. Stretch: custom API connection
209	
210	Ari could call a read-only DataTraceMind endpoint on the live URL and
211	pull cost figures on request. Attempt this only after DS-01 works end to
212	end and the EC2 instance is up.
213	
214	The **Add API** form ("Add an OpenAPI service Ari can use in this
215	workspace") asks for:
216	
217	| Field | Options |
218	|---|---|
219	| Display name | Free text |
220	| Authentication | Bearer token, API key header, Basic authentication, or No authentication |
221	| API key | The secret for the chosen method |
222	| OpenAPI specification | **Specification URL** or **Paste JSON**; version 3.0 or 3.1 per the docs |
223	| Advanced → Base URL | Only needed when the specification declares several servers |
224	
225	-   FastAPI serves an OpenAPI 3.1 document at `/openapi.json` by
226	    default, so no extra work is needed to produce one.
227	-   **Expose one read-only endpoint**, for example a unit-economics
228	    summary. Use **Paste JSON** with a specification trimmed to that
229	    path, so that inject, investigate, and approve are not described to
230	    cfo.ai at all.
231	-   **Give it its own bearer token.** Do not reuse the demo access code
232	    that guards inject, investigate, and approve. A human types the
233	    token into the form.
234	-   The public-URL guardrails in the brief (Section 4, "Live URL") still
235	    apply. Ari must never be able to send text that reaches a Codex
236	    prompt.
237	-   The value Ari reads is written into the Model as a plain number. It
238	    is a snapshot, not a live feed.
239	
240	------------------------------------------------------------------------
241	
242	## 7. Do not use
243	
244	-   **The `dtm` MCP server as a cfo.ai MCP connector.** It is a stdio
245	    server that Codex starts for each turn, and it holds the
246	    investigation tools and read-only database credentials. cfo.ai's
247	    **Add MCP server** form needs a secure URL, so the server would have
248	    to be re-hosted on the public internet. That contradicts the
249	    guardrails for the live URL.
250	-   **PostgreSQL or any other database integration.** Blocked by the
251	    plan (Section 4). Do not upgrade the plan to get it.
252	-   **A warehouse or ClickHouse workaround.** There is no ClickHouse
253	    connector, and the cfo.ai docs suggest a PostgreSQL-compatible
254	    database or a file upload instead. Use the file upload.
255	-   **Real-account connectors** (Stripe, QuickBooks, banking, payroll).
256	    The project has no such accounts, and connecting personal ones is
257	    out of scope.
258	
259	------------------------------------------------------------------------
260	
261	## 8. Human-only steps
262	
263	Coding agents stop and ask instead of attempting these, as in the
264	brief's "Steps only a human may perform".
265	
266	-   Signing in to cfo.ai and approving the OAuth request for the
267	    `cfoai` MCP server.
268	-   Anything under Settings → Billing or Settings → Usage.
269	-   Typing an API key or token into an **Add API** or **Add MCP server**
270	    form.
271	-   Uploading the CSV, unless the team leader asks an agent to do it in
272	    a browser session they have opened.
273	-   Answering Ari's onboarding question ("Where would you like to
274	    start?"), which is still open in the Welcome chat.
275	
276	------------------------------------------------------------------------
277	
278	## 9. Verified and not verified
279	
280	| Claim | Status |
281	|---|---|
282	| Plan is Startup (trial), canceled, ends 24 October 2026 | Verified in Settings → Billing |
283	| Standard 0 of 5, "Premium not included", no connections | Verified in Settings → Usage |
284	| PostgreSQL and its five hosted variants are tagged Premium | Verified in the in-app catalog |
285	| ClickHouse is not in the catalog | Verified ("No integrations found") |
286	| "Stripe (Direct)" is listed without a Premium tag | Verified in the in-app catalog |
287	| **Add API** form fields and its four authentication options | Verified in the app (form opened, not submitted) |
288	| **Add MCP server** form: name, secure URL, OAuth by default | Verified in the app (form opened, not submitted) |
289	| `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp` is live and requires OAuth | Verified: an unauthenticated request returns `401` with OAuth resource metadata |
290	| The app shows the same URL under "Connect via MCP" | Verified in Settings → Connections |
291	| MCP tool names, call shape, and limits | From cfo.ai docs; not tested (needs sign-in) |
292	| The MCP server works on a canceled trial until it ends | Not tested |
293	| `claude mcp add` and `codex mcp add` commands for `cfoai` | From cfo.ai docs; not run |
294	| CSV column-to-Variable and Dimension rules, 50 MB limit | From cfo.ai docs; not tested |
295	| Nightly sync at 02:00 UTC, 100-table limit | From cfo.ai docs; not tested |
296	| Custom API accepts a plain `http://` or bare-IP address | Not tested; the form's placeholders show `https://` |
297	| Bearer token and API key header options for a custom MCP server | From cfo.ai docs; only OAuth was seen in the form |
298	
299	When you verify or disprove a row, update this table.
300	
301	Sources: the cfo.ai app (connection manager and Settings, 10 October
302	2026); <https://cfo.ai/integrations>, <https://cfo.ai/agents>,
303	<https://cfo.ai/skill.md>, <https://cfo.ai/pricing>; the cfo.ai docs at
304	<https://docs.cfo.ai> (`integrations/connect-and-sync-data`,
305	`integrations/integrations-directory`, `integrations/mcp-server`,
306	`agent-instructions`, `workspace-settings/billing`); the hackathon guide
307	at <https://neatlogs.com/hackathon>; and an unauthenticated probe of the
308	MCP endpoint run on 10 October 2026.
309

plan for DataTraceMind or consider connecting anything to cfo.ai. Read

or exposing any DataTraceMind endpoint to cfo.ai.

**Status:** explored 10 October 2026 in the team leader's cfo.ai
workspace and the public cfo.ai docs. The path in Section 5 is a
**recommendation, not yet a decision**; when the team leader decides,
record it here and in `hackathon.md`. Nothing was connected or changed
in the workspace during the exploration. Section 9 lists what is

The product brief (`datatracemind_product_brief.md`, Section 4,

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Summary

-   The connector we would want, **PostgreSQL, is not available**: it is
    a Premium integration and this workspace's plan does not include
    Premium. **ClickHouse is not in the catalog at all.**
-   Three routes do work on this plan: cfo.ai's own MCP server (a coding
    agent reads and edits the model), CSV upload, and a custom API
    connection.
-   **Recommended:** the MCP server plus a CSV of per-investigation
    cost. The plan is then built from measured numbers instead of typed
    ones, which is what the brief asks for and what the 25% tooling
    score rewards.
-   The custom API connection is a stretch goal, only after DS-01 works
    end to end and the live URL is up.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2. The workspace

| Item | Observed 10 October 2026 |
|---|---|
| Workspace | "Divine Joey" (slug `divine-joey-f38178b9`) |
| Plan | Startup, on its trial; shown as Canceled, ends 24 October 2026 |
| Integration slots | Standard 0 of 5 used; "Premium not included" |
| Included AI usage | 0% used; resets 24 October 2026 |
| Extra usage | Purchased balance \$0.00; auto-reload off; monthly spend limit \$500.00 |
| Connections | None |

-   The trial ends after winners are announced on 16 October, so the
    workspace stays usable through judging. Per the cfo.ai billing docs,
    cancelling keeps the Model and its data; when the trial ends the
    workspace returns to the plan chooser.
-   The Startup plan, per the pricing page: up to 5 standard
    integrations, up to 500,000 rows synced per month, and the MCP
    server included.
-   Billing controls are human-only. Do not press **Keep Startup**,
    **Change**, **Buy credits**, or **Adjust limit**, and leave
    **Auto-reload** off.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3. Connection types

The connection manager opens from the sidebar (**Connections → +**) and
from **Settings → Connections**. It has three tabs and an **Upload**
button. cfo.ai's own MCP server is a fifth route that runs in the other
direction.

| Type | Where | How data arrives | Uses a plan slot |
|---|---|---|---|
| Integration | **Integrations** tab | Synced into the Model nightly, in a shared run that starts at 02:00 UTC | Yes |
| File upload | **Upload** button | One-off import of a `.csv`; never refreshes on its own | No |
| MCP connector | **MCP** tab | Ari calls the server live when asked; nothing is synced | No |
| API connection | **API** tab | Ari calls the API live when asked; nothing is synced | No |
| cfo.ai MCP server | Outside the app, at `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp` | An external agent reads and edits the Model | No; included in Startup |

-   **Integrations:** at most 100 tables per connection, and the table
    selection cannot be changed after setup. There is no manual refresh
    button; Ari can refresh a connection on request.
-   **Live connections (MCP, API):** a figure Ari looks up can be
    written into a Table Block as a plain value. It does not update
    afterwards.
-   **Secrets** for a connection are typed by a human into the secure
    field on the connection card. They are never pasted into the chat
    with Ari or into a coding-agent session.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4. Fit for DataTraceMind

| Connector | Fit | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| cfo.ai MCP server | **Use** | Builds pricing, costs, revenue, and runway from the coding agent, with base and growth as Scenarios |
| CSV upload | **Use** | Free, no slot, and carries measured cost per investigation into the Model |
| Custom API connection | Stretch | The FastAPI service can serve an OpenAPI document, so Ari could query a read-only cost endpoint on the live URL |
| Google Sheets | Possible, not planned | Standard, one slot, nightly refresh; more moving parts than CSV for no demo gain |
| PostgreSQL (also RDS, Aurora, Cloud SQL, Azure, Heroku) | **Blocked** | Tagged Premium in the catalog; the plan shows "Premium not included" |
| ClickHouse | **Not available** | Searching the catalog returns "No integrations found" |
| Custom MCP server pointing at `dtm` | **Do not use** | See Section 7 |
| Stripe, QuickBooks, HubSpot, and similar | Not relevant | The simulator has no real accounts behind it |

Even on a plan with Premium, the PostgreSQL connector would suit this
project poorly: it syncs once a night through Fivetran and needs a
database reachable from the internet, while ours runs in local Docker
Compose.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. Recommended path

### 5.1 cfo.ai MCP server

A coding agent connects to cfo.ai and builds the plan in the workspace.
This is a **development-time tool only**, like Entire. Never add it to
the `codex exec` invocation used by agent roles (see
`CODEX_LLM_PROVIDER.md`, Section 3); the product does not call cfo.ai.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Server name | `cfoai` |
| URL | `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp` |
| Transport | Remote Streamable HTTP |
| Authentication | OAuth in the browser, with the cfo.ai account |

``` sh
# Claude Code: then start claude, open /mcp, select cfoai, Authenticate
claude mcp add --transport http cfoai https://api.cfo.ai/mcp

# Codex
codex mcp add cfoai --url https://api.cfo.ai/mcp
codex mcp login cfoai
```

The browser sign-in and approval are human-only steps (Section 8).

-   **Workspace:** with one workspace the connection uses it. Otherwise
    call `list_orgs` and pass the workspace ID or slug as `org_id` on
    every later call.
-   **Read tools named in the docs:** `list_orgs`,
    `inspect_table_blocks`, `inspect_pages`, `inspect_scenarios`,
    `inspect_integrations`, `inspect_skills`, `inspect_canvas_library`,
    `inspect_dimension_mappings`, `inspect_history`,
    `inspect_documentation`.
-   **Write tools named in the docs:** `edit_table_blocks` (all model
    formulas go through it), `edit_pages`, `edit_scenarios`,
    `edit_dimension_mappings`, `edit_canvas_blocks`,
    `edit_integrations`, `edit_triggers`.
-   The cfo.ai docs pages do not list exactly the same tools. After
    sign-in, read the names and schemas from the server itself and
    follow <https://docs.cfo.ai/agent-instructions.md>.
-   **Call shape:** multi-action tools take one block named for the
    action, for example `{"read": {"target": "Operating Plan"}}`. There
    is no flat `action` field. One `read` takes up to 16 targets.

Rules when writing to the Model:

1.  **Inspect before changing.** Read the existing Model and the
    `build-model` skill (`inspect_skills`) first. Setup needs no writes;
    an empty workspace is a valid first read.
2.  **Writes change the live Model.** There is no separate approval
    step, so make only the change that was asked for.
3.  **Main is the base case.** Put the growth case in a separate
    Scenario (`edit_scenarios`), not in Main. That gives the two revenue
    scenarios the brief requires.
4.  **Label measured against assumed.** Cost per investigation comes
    from Section 5.2. Pricing, customer counts, and growth rates are
    assumptions and must be named as such in the Model.
5.  **Keep the evidence.** Export the plan or take screenshots into
    `business-plan/`, and note the session in `hackathon.md`.

A session that uses this server is captured by Entire like any other,
and checkpoints in a public repository are public. The plan is a
submission artifact, so that is acceptable; keep tokens out of the
session.

### 5.2 CSV of measured cost

The brief requires inference cost per investigation to come from real
runs. A small script exports one row per investigation, and a human
uploads the file.

-   **Source:** the token usage in each Codex turn's `turn.completed`
    event, summed per investigation (the same figures recorded on the
    neatlogs agent spans).
-   **Dollar figure:** an estimate at API list prices, computed as in
    `CODEX_LLM_PROVIDER.md`, Section 8. Name the column so that the
    estimate is obvious, for example `est_cost_usd`.
-   **Suggested columns:** `run_date`, `incident_id`, `scenario_id`,
    `workflow_version`, `role_turns`, `input_tokens`,
    `cached_input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `est_cost_usd`,
    `duration_s`.
-   **How cfo.ai reads columns:** numeric columns become summed
    Variables; text columns become Dimensions; a numeric column whose
    name marks an identifier (for example one ending in "id") loads as a
    text Dimension. Date columns are read per whole column.
-   **Upload:** the file must have a `.csv` extension and be at most
    50 MB. Choose **Use as a data source**, not **Use in chat only**.
    An Excel workbook is not accepted as a data source.
-   **Refresh:** uploads never refresh. They are tracked by filename;
    upload the file again to update it. Ingestion runs in the
    background, so ask Ari whether loading has finished.
-   Send summaries only: no source rows, customer data, prompts, or
    secrets.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 6. Stretch: custom API connection

Ari could call a read-only DataTraceMind endpoint on the live URL and
pull cost figures on request. Attempt this only after DS-01 works end to
end and the EC2 instance is up.

The **Add API** form ("Add an OpenAPI service Ari can use in this
workspace") asks for:

| Field | Options |
|---|---|
| Display name | Free text |
| Authentication | Bearer token, API key header, Basic authentication, or No authentication |
| API key | The secret for the chosen method |
| OpenAPI specification | **Specification URL** or **Paste JSON**; version 3.0 or 3.1 per the docs |
| Advanced → Base URL | Only needed when the specification declares several servers |

-   FastAPI serves an OpenAPI 3.1 document at `/openapi.json` by
    default, so no extra work is needed to produce one.
-   **Expose one read-only endpoint**, for example a unit-economics
    summary. Use **Paste JSON** with a specification trimmed to that
    path, so that inject, investigate, and approve are not described to
    cfo.ai at all.
-   **Give it its own bearer token.** Do not reuse the demo access code
    that guards inject, investigate, and approve. A human types the
    token into the form.
-   The public-URL guardrails in the brief (Section 4, "Live URL") still
    apply. Ari must never be able to send text that reaches a Codex
    prompt.
-   The value Ari reads is written into the Model as a plain number. It
    is a snapshot, not a live feed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 7. Do not use

-   **The `dtm` MCP server as a cfo.ai MCP connector.** It is a stdio
    server that Codex starts for each turn, and it holds the
    investigation tools and read-only database credentials. cfo.ai's
    **Add MCP server** form needs a secure URL, so the server would have
    to be re-hosted on the public internet. That contradicts the
    guardrails for the live URL.
-   **PostgreSQL or any other database integration.** Blocked by the
    plan (Section 4). Do not upgrade the plan to get it.
-   **A warehouse or ClickHouse workaround.** There is no ClickHouse
    connector, and the cfo.ai docs suggest a PostgreSQL-compatible
    database or a file upload instead. Use the file upload.
-   **Real-account connectors** (Stripe, QuickBooks, banking, payroll).
    The project has no such accounts, and connecting personal ones is
    out of scope.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 8. Human-only steps

Coding agents stop and ask instead of attempting these, as in the
brief's "Steps only a human may perform".

-   Signing in to cfo.ai and approving the OAuth request for the
    `cfoai` MCP server.
-   Anything under Settings → Billing or Settings → Usage.
-   Typing an API key or token into an **Add API** or **Add MCP server**
    form.
-   Uploading the CSV, unless the team leader asks an agent to do it in
    a browser session they have opened.
-   Answering Ari's onboarding question ("Where would you like to
    start?"), which is still open in the Welcome chat.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Local stack for DataTraceMind. One PostgreSQL instance holds the
# operational source (schema `oltp`) and the analytics target (schema
# `analytics`); the app creates schemas, roles, and seed data itself.
#
# The passwords below are defaults for a disposable local database. Override
# them through the environment on any machine that is reachable by others.
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: dtm_admin
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DTM_POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-dtm_local_dev}
      POSTGRES_DB: datatracemind
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${DTM_POSTGRES_PORT:-5432}:5432"
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U dtm_admin -d datatracemind"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

volumes:
  pgdata:

-- Analytics target. Applied once per target schema: `analytics` (the demo
-- environment) and `staging` (rebuilt for every repair validation run).
-- __TARGET__ is replaced with the schema name by datatracemind.db.
--
-- Fact tables deliberately have no unique constraint on the business key.
-- Uniqueness is the load step's job (replace-by-key) and is verified by a
-- data-quality check, so a non-idempotent load shows up as duplicates
-- instead of being masked by the database.

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS __TARGET__;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS __TARGET__.fact_orders (
    row_id            BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    order_id          BIGINT NOT NULL,
    customer_id       BIGINT NOT NULL,
    order_status      TEXT NOT NULL,
    total_amount      NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL,
    currency          CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
    order_date        DATE NOT NULL,
    payment_count     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    captured_amount   NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL,
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    etl_run_id        BIGINT NOT NULL,
    transform_version INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS __TARGET__.fact_payments (
    row_id            BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    payment_id        BIGINT NOT NULL,
    order_id          BIGINT NOT NULL,
    payment_status    TEXT NOT NULL,
    amount            NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL,
    currency          CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
    paid_at           TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    revenue_date      DATE NOT NULL,
    is_revenue        BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
    etl_run_id        BIGINT NOT NULL,
    transform_version INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS __TARGET__.fact_refunds (
    row_id            BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    refund_id         BIGINT NOT NULL,
    payment_id        BIGINT NOT NULL,
    order_id          BIGINT NOT NULL,
    refund_status     TEXT NOT NULL,
    refund_amount     NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL,
    currency          CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    revenue_date      DATE NOT NULL,
    is_subtracted     BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
    subtracted_amount NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL,
    etl_run_id        BIGINT NOT NULL,
    transform_version INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS fact_orders_order_idx ON __TARGET__.fact_orders (order_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS fact_payments_order_idx ON __TARGET__.fact_payments (order_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS fact_refunds_order_idx ON __TARGET__.fact_refunds (order_id);

-- One row per business day and currency; rebuilt from the fact tables.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS __TARGET__.daily_revenue (
    revenue_date      DATE NOT NULL,
    currency          CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
    gross_paid_amount NUMERIC(14, 2) NOT NULL,
    refund_amount     NUMERIC(14, 2) NOT NULL,
    net_revenue       NUMERIC(14, 2) NOT NULL,
    order_count       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    refreshed_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    transform_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (revenue_date, currency)
);

-- status: RUNNING | SUCCESS | FAILED
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS __TARGET__.etl_run_log (
    run_id            BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    trigger           TEXT NOT NULL,
    started_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    finished_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,
    status            TEXT NOT NULL,
    transform_version INTEGER,
    full_refresh      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    extracted_count   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    transformed_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    rejected_count    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    loaded_count      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    watermark         TIMESTAMPTZ,
    error_summary     TEXT,
    details           JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS __TARGET__.data_quality_results (
    result_id          BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    run_id             BIGINT NOT NULL,
    check_name         TEXT NOT NULL,
    passed             BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
    severity           TEXT NOT NULL,
    observed_value     JSONB NOT NULL,
    expected_condition TEXT NOT NULL,
    checked_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS data_quality_results_run_idx ON __TARGET__.data_quality_results (run_id);

-- High-water mark of the last successful load, and the transform version
-- that produced the current fact rows.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS __TARGET__.etl_checkpoint (
    pipeline_name     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    watermark         TIMESTAMPTZ,
    transform_version INTEGER,
    last_run_id       BIGINT,
    updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- DataTraceMind's own state: incidents, the agent timeline, evidence, repair
-- proposals, approvals, and the audit log. This is the application's record
-- for the UI and for approval enforcement; it does not depend on trace
-- export. The read-only investigation role has no access to this schema, so
-- agents cannot read scenario ground truth or approval state through SQL.

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS dtm;

CREATE SEQUENCE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.incident_seq;
CREATE SEQUENCE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.proposal_seq;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.incidents (
    incident_id    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    incident_type  TEXT NOT NULL,
    severity       TEXT NOT NULL,
    status         TEXT NOT NULL,
    summary        TEXT NOT NULL,
    detected_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    resolved_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    trigger        JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    source_metrics JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    target_metrics JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    -- Workflow state that has no table of its own: hypotheses, the selected
    -- root cause, applicable business rules, errors, trace references.
    state          JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    -- Evaluator-only: which lab scenario was active at detection. Never put
    -- in a prompt or a tool result.
    scenario_id    TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.agent_events (
    event_id    BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    incident_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dtm.incidents (incident_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    agent       TEXT NOT NULL,
    event_type  TEXT NOT NULL,
    status      TEXT NOT NULL,
    summary     TEXT NOT NULL,
    payload     JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS agent_events_incident_idx ON dtm.agent_events (incident_id, event_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.evidence (
    incident_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dtm.incidents (incident_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    evidence_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind           TEXT NOT NULL,
    source         TEXT NOT NULL,
    description    TEXT NOT NULL,
    query_or_tool  TEXT NOT NULL,
    arguments      JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    result_summary JSONB NOT NULL,
    collected_by   TEXT NOT NULL,
    observed_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (incident_id, evidence_id)
);

-- status: proposed | validated | validation_failed | approved | rejected
--         | applied | verified | application_failed | superseded
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.repair_proposals (
    proposal_id       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    incident_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dtm.incidents (incident_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    target_file       TEXT NOT NULL,
    base_version      INTEGER NOT NULL,
    base_hash         TEXT NOT NULL,
    new_content       TEXT NOT NULL,
    diff              TEXT NOT NULL,
    patch_hash        TEXT NOT NULL,
    rationale         TEXT NOT NULL,
    risk              TEXT NOT NULL,
    rollback_plan     TEXT NOT NULL,
    cited_evidence    JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
    status            TEXT NOT NULL,
    validation_result JSONB,
    post_fix_result   JSONB,
    applied_version   INTEGER,
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- One row per human decision. Approval is bound to the patch hash recorded
-- here; the executor compares it with the proposal's current hash.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.approvals (
    approval_id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    incident_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dtm.incidents (incident_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    proposal_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dtm.repair_proposals (proposal_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    patch_hash  TEXT NOT NULL,
    decision    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (decision IN ('approved', 'rejected')),
    actor       TEXT NOT NULL,
    reason      TEXT,
    decided_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.audit_log (
    audit_id   BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    actor      TEXT NOT NULL,
    action     TEXT NOT NULL,
    target     TEXT NOT NULL,
    result     TEXT NOT NULL,
    details    JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.alerts (
    alert_id    BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    incident_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dtm.incidents (incident_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    severity    TEXT NOT NULL,
    title       TEXT NOT NULL,
    body        JSONB NOT NULL,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- One row per investigation run: what the before/after comparison and the
-- cost-per-investigation export are built from.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.investigation_runs (
    run_id              BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    incident_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dtm.incidents (incident_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    scenario_id         TEXT,
    workflow_version    TEXT NOT NULL,
    model               TEXT NOT NULL,
    trace_id            TEXT,
    status              TEXT NOT NULL,
    started_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    finished_at         TIMESTAMPTZ,
    duration_s          NUMERIC(10, 2),
    role_turns          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    tool_calls          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    failed_tool_calls   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    retries             INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    input_tokens        BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    cached_input_tokens BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    output_tokens       BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    est_cost_usd        NUMERIC(10, 4) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

-- Scenario lab state (single row). Evaluator/demo-harness only.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.lab_state (
    id                     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT 1 CHECK (id = 1),
    scenario_id            TEXT,
    injected_at            TIMESTAMPTZ,
    baseline_metrics       JSONB,
    post_injection_metrics JSONB
);

INSERT INTO dtm.lab_state (id) VALUES (1) ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING;

# Local stack for DataTraceMind. One PostgreSQL instance holds the
# operational source (schema `oltp`) and the analytics target (schema
# `analytics`); the app creates schemas, roles, and seed data itself.
#
# The passwords below are defaults for a disposable local database. Override
# them through the environment on any machine that is reachable by others.
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: dtm_admin
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DTM_POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-dtm_local_dev}
      POSTGRES_DB: datatracemind
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${DTM_POSTGRES_PORT:-5432}:5432"
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U dtm_admin -d datatracemind"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

volumes:
  pgdata:

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.repair_proposals (
    proposal_id       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    incident_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dtm.incidents (incident_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    target_file       TEXT NOT NULL,
    base_version      INTEGER NOT NULL,
    base_hash         TEXT NOT NULL,
    new_content       TEXT NOT NULL,
    diff              TEXT NOT NULL,
    patch_hash        TEXT NOT NULL,
    rationale         TEXT NOT NULL,
    risk              TEXT NOT NULL,
    rollback_plan     TEXT NOT NULL,
    cited_evidence    JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
    status            TEXT NOT NULL,
    validation_result JSONB,
    post_fix_result   JSONB,
    applied_version   INTEGER,
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- One row per human decision. Approval is bound to the patch hash recorded
-- here; the executor compares it with the proposal's current hash.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.approvals (
    approval_id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    incident_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dtm.incidents (incident_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    proposal_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dtm.repair_proposals (proposal_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    patch_hash  TEXT NOT NULL,
    decision    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (decision IN ('approved', 'rejected')),
    actor       TEXT NOT NULL,
    reason      TEXT,
    decided_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.audit_log (
    audit_id   BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    actor      TEXT NOT NULL,
    action     TEXT NOT NULL,
    target     TEXT NOT NULL,
    result     TEXT NOT NULL,
    details    JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.alerts (
    alert_id    BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    incident_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dtm.incidents (incident_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    severity    TEXT NOT NULL,
    title       TEXT NOT NULL,
    body        JSONB NOT NULL,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- One row per investigation run: what the before/after comparison and the
-- cost-per-investigation export are built from.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dtm.investigation_runs (
    run_id              BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    incident_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES dtm.incidents (incident_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    scenario_id         TEXT,
    workflow_version    TEXT NOT NULL,
    model               TEXT NOT NULL,
    trace_id            TEXT,
    status              TEXT NOT NULL,
    started_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    finished_at         TIMESTAMPTZ,
    duration_s          NUMERIC(10, 2),
    role_turns          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    tool_calls          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    failed_tool_calls   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    retries             INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    input_tokens        BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    cached_input_tokens BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    output_tokens       BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    est_cost_usd        NUMERIC(10, 4) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

    id                     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT 1 CHECK (id = 1),
    scenario_id            TEXT,
    injected_at            TIMESTAMPTZ,
    baseline_metrics       JSONB,
    post_injection_metrics JSONB
);

owner: demo finance policy (the approved definition for this environment)
rules:
  payment_statuses_included: [CAPTURED]
  refund_statuses_subtracted: [SUCCEEDED]
  refund_amount_basis: refund_amount
